newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SHOWGIRL PIERCE PROVES SHE'S A WINNER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SHOWGIRL PIERCE PROVES SHE'S A WINNER.

text.p: Mary Pierce has rediscovered the 'arm-pump' gesture of jubilation she made famous two years ago but this time around it comes from the heart.

The 22-year-old Frenchwoman, one of the crowd favourites at the Australian Open, produced her best grand slam result since lifting the title in Melbourne two years ago when she came back from the brink of defeat on Tuesday to reach the semifinals.

"A year or two ago I probably would have lost this match, so I feel very good...even though I didn't feel good or play good," Pierce said after recovering from a set down to beat 16th seed Sabine Appelmans of Belgium.
The former world number three took a three-month break from tennis late last year to sort herself out mentally and have treatment for a shoulder injury. She has returned with a winning attitude.

The strut, frown, toss of the head, cry of anguish, laugh and smile are all back on show. And the arm-pump was back on Tuesday, too -- starting from shoulder-height carrying all the way through, her fist striking the court.
Pierce is a performer -- like recently retired Gabriela Sabatini, she creates an aura on court.
But she has added a new tune to her repertoire, the ability to fight when faced with defeat, twice recovering from a one-set deficit to win in Melbourne.
On Tuesday Pierce lost the first set 6-1 before capturing the second and then came back from 3-0 down in the last to win 1-6 6-4 6-4 in just over two hours.
Pierce said in the past she had been a strong starter but was prone to succumbing under pressure.
"I guess I have more experience and maturity and I'm not freaking out," she said.
Pierce has been one of the crowd favourites in Melbourne, where she has shown regular flashes of the form which won her the title in 1995, her last major victory.
Where Spain's Carlos Moya has attracted a strong following among Melbourne teenage girls, Pierce is the boys' favourite.
"It's just a good feeling to know that they appreciate what you do and all the hard work that you've done has paid off and they're enjoying the match," said Pierce.
Her next opponent will be South African 12th seed Amanda Coetzer, conqueror of world number one Steffi Graf on Sunday.
